p: יוֹם זֶה נִקְרָא הִלּוּלָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי
This day is called the Hilula of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
because on this day he passed away.
Now, although we find that they established a fast
on the day of the death of tzaddikim,
as on the seventh of Adar,
the passing of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
where, although it is Rosh Chodesh,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא יוֹם פְּטִירַת אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן
because it is the day of the passing of Aharon HaKohen
וְטוּר וְשׁוּלְחָן עָרוּךְ אוֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן תקפ)
and the Tur and Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 580),
וְלָמָּה בִּפְטִירַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי
why, at the passing of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
did they make a Yom Tov?
But the reason they established a fast
on the day of the death of tzaddikim
דַּוְקָא בְּצַדִּיקִים שֶׁהָיוּ מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב
applies specifically to tzaddikim who were of the root of Torah she'bichsav;
and where we find a fast for tzaddikim
at the death of those executed by the government,
it is because they were killed
and did not die in their beds.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
was the root of Torah she'bichsav,
וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and Rabbi Akiva was the root of Torah she'b'al peh
(as is stated in the writings of the Arizal).
And it is stated in the Midrash
When their masters are gathered from them;
as long as his teacher is alive," etc.
And on the day he passed away,
the words of Torah then became fixed
in the hearts of Yisrael, his students.
וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי הָיָה תַּלְמִיד רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was the student of Rabbi Akiva,
for my measures are the choicest of the choicest
of the measures of Rabbi Akiva";
that is, the root of the teachings of Rabbi Akiva.
And this was on Lag BaOmer,
in the sefirah of Hod sheb'Hod,
for Hod is the attribute of Aharon HaKohen,
since the seven shepherds correspond to the seven attributes
וְהוּא הָיָה גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and he too was the root of Torah she'b'al peh.
For Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
was the root of Torah she'bichsav,
and Aharon the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן וְגוֹמֵר
as it says, "For the lips of the Kohen," etc.,
"and Torah they shall seek from his mouth";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהוּא יִהְיֶה לְּךָ לְפֶה
and as it says, "And he shall be for you a mouth."
And the sefirah of Hod sheb'Hod
is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
of the measures of Rabbi Akiva."
And the day of his passing
נִקְרָא הִילּוּלָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי
is called the Hilula of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
for all of Yisrael in his generation
received, and there became fixed in their hearts then,
as they said in the Midrash,
"When their masters are gathered from them."
And on the fourteenth of Iyar, Pesach Sheni,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קנב, ב)
as is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 152b):
"The first Pesach is from the right,
the second Pesach from the left," etc.,
"and on the right, where Torah she'bichsav is," etc.
is the root of the attribute of Aharon,
שֶׁהוּא אוֹהֵב אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת וּמְקָרְבָן לַתּוֹרָה
who loves people and brings them close to Torah,
who was the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
who would expound the crowns of the letters
And it is stated in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Chukas 8):
"Things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues;
'and every precious thing his eye beheld' —
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."
as they expounded in the Gemara (Megillah 16b):
"'Precious' — these are the tefillin of the head,"
which are on top, like a crown.
But they could not establish the day of the Hilula
on the day of Rabbi Akiva's passing,
And about this they said (Menachos there),
"Thus it arose in thought before Me,"
meaning that he was from the root of thought.
And he was called Akiva ben Yosef,
for he was like Mashiach ben Yosef,
of whom it is stated in the Gemara (Sukkah 52a)
וּמִן הַסְּתָם הָיָה נִצְרָךְ לִהְיוֹת כֵּן
and presumably it had to be so
and so too it had to be with Rabbi Akiva.
בְּיוֹם פְּטִירַת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי
on the day of the passing of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
in whom was the choicest of the choicest
of the measures of Rabbi Akiva.
וּמִן הַסְּתָם נוֹלַד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי
And presumably Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was born
as they proved in the Gemara (Kiddushin 38a):
וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁבְּשִׁבְעָה בַּאֲדָר נוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵּי
"And from where do we know that Moshe was born on the seventh of Adar," etc.,
"that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and fills
וְלָכֵן בְּיוֹם זֶה יָרְדָה נֶפֶשׁ זֶה
Therefore on this day there descended this soul
which was the root of Torah she'b'al peh.
And therefore it is stated in the Yerushalmi (Sanhedrin 1:2)
דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחָאי
that Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai,
"It is enough for you that I and your Creator recognize your strength";
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה שׁוּם אָדָם מַכִּיר כֹּחוֹ
for no person recognized his strength
רַק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
except the Holy One, blessed be He, and Rabbi Akiva,
who was the root of Torah she'b'al peh.
And every year, when this day comes,
יָכוֹל כָּל אָדָם לִזְכּוֹת לְפִי כֹּחוֹ
every person can merit, according to his capacity,
to attain the fixing of the words of Torah
and therefore they established it as a festival.
